objects.name: Cepheus Flare

source.reference: Zucker, C., Speagle, J. S., Schlafly, E. F., et al. 2019, ApJ, 879, 125, 'A Large Catalog of Accurate Distances to Local Molecular Clouds: The Gaia DR2 Edition' (arXiv:1902.01425) - 'Cepheus Near' cloud component: 352 pc +/- 1 pc (statistical) +/- 18 pc (systematic); error_pc here is the quadrature sum of the two quoted terms.
source.catalog: Zucker et al. 2019 (Gaia DR2 3D dust-based molecular cloud distances)

objects.notes: Position (ra/dec) taken from the SIMBAD entry 'NAME Cepheus Flare' (otype MoC), the closest single-point designation SIMBAD offers for the complex; SIMBAD carries no parallax/distance for this extended entry, so distance is taken from Zucker et al. 2019 instead (spec S10: prefer Gaia-era literature to a stale/missing SIMBAD distance). The Cepheus Flare is in reality several individually Gaia-resolved dark clouds (L1148, L1158, L1177, L1217, L1219, L1235, L1251, L1228) spanning 330-368 pc (Dzib et al. 2021, MNRAS, 505, 5164, 'The Gaia view of the Cepheus flare', arXiv:2105.10039); the complex also spans ~90x60 pc in the plane of the sky per that paper (visual.size_pc uses the larger axis). This record collapses that structure to one MVP centroid using the Zucker et al. 2019 'Cepheus Near' value, which falls within the Dzib range.

objects.name: Local Bubble

source.reference: Alves, M.I.R., Boulanger, F., Ferriere, K. & Montier, L. (2018), "The Local Bubble: a magnetic veil to our Galaxy", A&A, 611, L5 (doi:10.1051/0004-6361/201832637). Center position reused from Story #62's models/local_bubble.yaml ellipsoid-model center_pc = (x=10.2, y=33.6, z=0.0) pc, itself Alves et al. (2018) Table 1's fitted off-centred-spheroid offset (Sun at 0.58 of the semi-minor axis from the ellipsoid centre, along l=73 deg, b~0 deg) scaled by the paper's approximate a_pc=60 pc physical anchor (Sec. 1, citing Puspitarini et al. 2014, A&A, 566, A13).

objects.notes: This is a single-point/centroid catalog-object representation of the Local Bubble (spec Idea.md §9 seed list, §15 MVP 'center + approximate radius' allowance), distinct from the separate, more detailed ellipsoid geometry in Story #62's models/local_bubble.yaml (which this entry deliberately does not duplicate or modify). No formal uncertainty is available for the centroid position itself in the source (Alves et al. 2018 fit shape/orientation, not an absolute distance, with error bars only on the dimensionless shape parameters - see models/local_bubble.yaml for those); the 60 pc anchor behind this position, and visual.size_pc here (approximating the semi-minor axis as a representative radius), are both order-of-magnitude, not precision-fit, figures. Position/distance were reverse-derived from center_pc via astropy Galactic->ICRS and round-trip verified to reproduce x=10.2, y=33.6, z=0.0 pc through this project's own coordinates.derive_galactic_coordinates().

objects.name: Orion OB1

source.reference: Kounkel, M., Hartmann, L., Loinard, L., et al. 2018, AJ, 156, 84, 'The APOGEE-2 Survey of the Orion Star-forming Complex. II. Six-dimensional Structure' (arXiv:1805.04649) - kinematic group 'Orion D' (the population tracing the classical OB1a/OB1b belt stars, extending toward Rigel): 350 +/- 3 pc from APOGEE-2 + Gaia DR2 astrometry.

objects.notes: SIMBAD's entry for this association is 'NAME Ori I' (otype As*; ra/dec taken from that entry) - Blaauw's original Roman-numeral naming for Orion's first-catalogued OB association, i.e. Orion OB1. Kounkel et al. 2018 find the classical OB1a/OB1b sky-area boundaries (Blaauw 1964: 199<l<210 deg, -21<b<-12 deg) do not cleanly map onto their kinematically distinct groups; their 'Orion D' group is the closest match to the OB1a/OB1b belt population and is used here as the representative distance. A separate, foreground-superimposed kinematic group 'Orion C' (the sigma Ori cluster, part of classical OB1b) sits at 406 +/- 4 pc in the same paper and is not separately represented in this MVP record.

objects.name: Scorpius-Centaurus Association

source.reference: de Zeeuw, P. T., Hoogerwerf, R., de Bruijne, J. H. J., Brown, A. G. A., Blaauw, A. 1999, AJ, 117, 354, 'A HIPPARCOS Census of the Nearby OB Associations' - mean subgroup distances: Upper Scorpius (US) 145 pc, Upper Centaurus-Lupus (UCL) 140 pc, Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) 118 pc. Still the standard subgroup-distance reference used by Gaia-era Sco-Cen studies (e.g. Damiani, F., et al. 2019, A&A, 623, A112, arXiv:1807.11884, which restricts its Gaia DR2 census to <200 pc and finds ~90% of known massive members within 100-170 pc, consistent with these subgroup values rather than superseding them with one number).
source.catalog: Hipparcos (de Zeeuw et al. 1999); consistent with Gaia DR2 (Damiani et al. 2019)

objects.notes: Sco-Cen is the nearest OB association to the Sun but comprises 3 kinematically/spatially distinct subgroups (Upper Sco, Upper Cen-Lup, Lower Cen-Crux) spanning tens of pc in depth - the current schema has no sub-group representation, so this is deliberately simplified to a single MVP centroid, per issue #59 guidance. distance_pc is the unweighted mean of the 3 published subgroup distances (134.3 pc); distance.error_pc is the population standard deviation across those 3 subgroups (11.7 pc) - this is a depth-spread proxy, NOT a formal parallax/fit uncertainty, and should not be conflated with one. Position (ra/dec) is taken from the SIMBAD entry 'NAME Upper Sco-Cen' (otype As*), the closest single-point designation SIMBAD offers for the complex as a whole. A future story could add the 3 subgroups as separate records with `group.primary` set to this association's id.

objects.name: Vela Supernova Remnant

source.reference: Dodson, R., Legge, D., Reynolds, J.E. & McCulloch, P.M. (2003), "The Vela Pulsar's Proper Motion and Parallax Derived from VLBI Observations", ApJ, 596, 1137 (arXiv:astro-ph/0302374). VLBI parallax of the embedded pulsar PSR B0833-45 = 3.4 +/- 0.2 mas, equivalent to a distance of 293 (+19/-17) pc; adopted here as the remnant's distance per standard convention that the Vela SNR shares the distance of its associated pulsar.

objects.notes: Coordinates are those of the embedded pulsar PSR B0833-45 (SIMBAD 'NAME Vela Pulsar'), ~0.4 deg from the SIMBAD-catalogued extended-remnant centroid ('NAME Vela', SNR G263.9-03.3; ra=128.5, dec=-45.833) - within the remnant's ~4 deg angular radius and negligible (~2 pc) at this distance. error_pc uses the larger (+19 pc) of the source's asymmetric +19/-17 pc uncertainty, since this schema's error_pc is a single symmetric value. visual.size_pc ~= 40 pc is an approximate physical diameter derived from the remnant's commonly quoted ~8 deg angular diameter (ROSAT X-ray survey era literature, e.g. Aschenbach 1998 and successors) at the adopted VLBI distance - an order-of-magnitude figure, not a formally fitted size.

source.reference: Perrot, C. A. & Grenier, I. A. (2003), "3D dynamical evolution of the interstellar gas in the Gould Belt", Astronomy & Astrophysics, 404, 519-531
source.notes: Center XYZ derived from the paper's reported (distance=104pc, l=180.4deg, b=0) via this repo's Galactic Cartesian convention (spec §6); orientation_deg is the paper's ascending-node longitude l_Omega=296.1deg. All other fields are the paper's fitted values verbatim (see comments above).

source.reference: Konietzka, R., Goodman, A. A., Zucker, C., Burkert, A., Alves, J., Foley, M., Swiggum, C., Koller, M. & Miret-Roig, N. (2024), "The Radcliffe Wave is oscillating", Nature, 626, 63-68
source.notes: arXiv:2402.12596. Points are the paper's own published best-fit model spine (file 'Radcliffe_Wave_best_fit_model_Konietzka2024.tab', CC0-licensed), i.e. the fitted/interpolated curve, not raw individual cloud or cluster measurements - see 'curve_type' and this module's docstring. Raw file kept unmodified at data/raw/Radcliffe_Wave_best_fit_model_Konietzka2024.tab (spec §13). s_pc is this repo's own derived cumulative 3D arclength along the file's point ordering (not a column in the source file). The source file's x, y, z columns are stated by the paper (Methods, 'Full Spatial and Kinematic Model') to be Heliocentric Galactic Cartesian coordinates, matching spec §6's convention; the source file's fourth column, vz (line-of-sight velocity), is not part of this Story's spatial schema and is not carried into models/radcliffe_wave.csv.

radcliffe_wave.notes: This is the interpolated/fitted Radcliffe Wave curve (Konietzka et al. 2024's published best-fit spine), not observed cloud positions. It does not replace the individual astronomical objects (e.g. Taurus, Perseus, Orion) that make up the Wave - those are separate catalog entries (spec §7) tracked elsewhere.

source.reference: Alves, M.I.R., Boulanger, F., Ferriere, K. & Montier, L. (2018), "The Local Bubble: a magnetic veil to our Galaxy", Astronomy & Astrophysics, 611, L5. Table 1 gives the fitted shape (aspect ratio c_ell/a_ell = 2.7 +/- 0.6), orientation (Euler angles, and the long axis pointing towards l=216 deg, b=60 deg), and the Sun's offset as a fraction of the semi-minor axis (0.58, along l=73 deg, b~0 deg) - all obtained by fitting an off-centred prolate-spheroid shell model to Planck 353 GHz dust polarization observations of the Galactic polar caps.
source.secondary_reference: IMPORTANT CAVEAT on absolute scale: dust polarization data alone carry no distance information, so Alves et al. (2018) fit their spheroid in normalized units with the semi-minor axis fixed to 1 (aell = bell = 1, set - see their Table 1 and Sec. 3). The `semi_axes_pc` and `center_pc` values in this file were produced by multiplying those dimensionless, precisely-fitted shape/orientation /offset-fraction numbers by an approximate physical scale anchor of a_pc = 60 pc, taken from the paper's own Sec. 1 description of the Local Bubble "extending out to ~60 pc towards the Galactic centre ... (Puspitarini et al. 2014)" - itself citing Puspitarini, R., Lallement, R., Vergely, J.-L. & Snowden, S.L. (2014), Astronomy & Astrophysics, 566, A13. This 60 pc anchor is an approximate, order-of-magnitude figure, not a quantity fitted jointly with the shape/orientation parameters above - treat `semi_axes_pc` and `center_pc` as illustrative-scale, not precision-fit, values.

local_bubble.notes: MVP simplified volume per spec Idea.md §18. A coarse off-centred spheroid approximation of the Local Bubble shell, intended to be replaced by a more realistic 3D reconstruction later without renderer changes (see module docstring in local_bubble.py for the intended extension path).
